title: Outsiders Pay $6,500 for Help With Sorority Rush
summary: The push by young women to gain acceptance into sororities at large schools in the Deep South has led to an increase in demand for rush coaches. Bloomberg News Reporter Gabriel Baumgaertner discusses his recent story about the high price tag some parents are willing to invest to help their kids get into the sorority of their dreams. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Trump Touts $3B in Mineral Project to Counter China
summary: During a recent meeting with top industry executives, the US President announced $3 billion in investments aimed at strengthening the domestic critical minerals and mining sector. The initiative seeks to reduce reliance on supply chains dominated by China. Gary Evans, Chairman and CEO of US Antimony, participated in the discussion and spoke to Bloomberg News about how much he is willing to see the government invest in his firm. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Gotham Greens CEO: Not Good To Have an Outbreak Like This
summary: Craig Stevenson, CEO of Gotham Greens, addressed the ongoing concerns over food safety amid recent recalls linked to salmonella in jalapenos and the widespread Cyclospora outbreak affecting thousands in the U.S. He noted a temporary decline in consumer demand for greens as news of outbreaks circulates, but emphasized that consumer interest in salads remains strong. He speaks with David Gura & Isabelle Lee on "The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Emerging Currencies Weaken as US-Iran Standoff Lifts Dollar

(Source: Bloomberg)

title: US Stocks End Mixed as Chipmaker Earnings, CPI Due to Set Pace
summary: US stocks held steady through Monday’s market close after a strong earnings week as investors continue to navigate the uncertain path of interest rates and war in Iran. The market is gearing up for the final stretch of corporate earnings, with chipmakers set to provide confirmation for the long-winded debate over valuations.

title: Hoenig: Upcoming Data Will Be Deciding Factor for Fed
summary: Thomas Hoenig, Distinguished Senior Fellow at the Mercatus Center, discussed the Federal Reserve's current stance amid recent economic data. He emphasized that the Fed is maintaining a cautious, wait-and-see attitude as it awaits upcoming inflation reports, including CPI and PPI data, which will be critical for shaping future policy decisions. He speaks with David Gura & Isabelle Lee on "The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)

title: US High-Grade Bond Market Sees Most Issuers Since January
summary: A record pace in US investment-grade bond issuance continued Monday with 19 firms storming the market, the most in seven months.

title: Dating App Grindr Unveils New AI Features, Premium Tier
summary: Grindr CEO George Arison said that new AI features and premium tiers are popular with users but that the company is still working out how to price the optional upgrades. Arison said that when it comes to the app's AI rollout, information gathered by AI can help users feel more comfortable meeting up with matches from farther away, especially in areas outside of cities that have a lower density gay population.  (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Latest Oil Market News and Analysis for Aug. 10
